---
title: "Study dataset build"
date: now
date-format: "YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm"
# Carried in the file rather than inherited from _quarto.yml, as every template
# is: a file meant to be copied must not depend on the directory it sits in.
format:
  html:
    fig-width: 9
    fig-height: 6
    theme: cosmo
    toc: true
    toc-location: left
    page-layout: full
    grid:
      body-width: 2000px
      sidebar-width: 250px
    toc-depth: 3
    df-print: default
    embed-resources: true
# A build report shows no code, where other templates fold it. This job's
# EXCLUDE rules may name patients, and the source of a folded chunk is in the
# HTML, which gets shared. The report is read for its counts; reviewers read
# this file. The setup chunk suppresses warnings and messages; later chunks send
# them to the console instead.
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false
  message: false
---

<!-- EDIT: name the SAS job this replaces (usually datasets/bd.data.sas) and the master it read. -->

This job cuts the study's dataset from a master
snapshot, records who was excluded and why, and writes the study's working
dataset with its build record beside it. When `REGISTER` is `TRUE` it registers
that file as a dated version of this study's `"built"` dataset (also called
`"study"`), the one every analysis job reads.

Before it registers, the job checks what it built: what the rebuild changed
against the version registered now, cross-tabs, the follow-up columns and the
study's own named checks. The report holds their counts; the rows behind them
go to the console, never into the report.

What does not belong here: corrections to a patient's values (they belong to
the master's corrections, in hvtiRdatabuild, so every study sees them);
imputation, propensity scores and variables for one model (a `vars` job).

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| results: asis
# unnumbered: defines .bd_table(), whose callers carry their own tbl- labels and captions
# add_job() writes SUBJECT and TYPE from the file's name; a hand-edited
# declaration that drifts from it stops the render in .job_setup().
SUBJECT <- "study"
TYPE    <- "build"
.in <- knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)
# Quarto knits through an intermediate, so the name is put back to .qmd.
.job_file <- if (is.null(.in)) "this job" else sub("[.][^.]+$", ".qmd", basename(.in))
# Every stop names its step and this file, and never a data value.
.bd_stop <- function(step, ...) stop("bd: ", step, " (", .job_file, "): ", ..., call. = FALSE)
# Registering claims the build record only from hvtiRutilities 1.5.3, and declaring the working file
# (declare_data()) needs 1.5.12; an older one would record a bd cut as legacy or cannot declare it. The named
# checks need proc_print(), released in 1.5.17, and the rebuild comparison compare_built(), in hvtiRdatabuild 0.3.3.
if (utils::packageVersion("hvtiRutilities") < "1.5.17") {
  .bd_stop("setup", "this job needs hvtiRutilities >= 1.5.17 for proc_print(); ",
           utils::packageVersion("hvtiRutilities"), " is installed.")
}
if (!requireNamespace("hvtiRdatabuild", quietly = TRUE) || utils::packageVersion("hvtiRdatabuild") < "0.3.3") {
  .bd_stop("setup", "this job needs hvtiRdatabuild >= 0.3.3 for compare_built().")
}
# Later chunks send warnings and messages to the console rather than the report.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(warning = NA, message = NA)
# One numbered table, for a section that shows a table only when it has one or shows several: a
# child chunk with its own label and caption while rendering, and a plain table in the console,
# where a child's label would collide with the same chunk run before.
.bd_table <- function(tab, label, cap, ...) {
  if (!isTRUE(getOption("knitr.in.progress"))) return(print(knitr::kable(tab, ...)))
  child <- new.env(parent = environment())
  fence <- strrep("`", 3)
  cat(knitr::knit_child(text = c(paste0(fence, "{r}"), paste0("#| label: ", label),
                                 paste0("#| tbl-cap: ", encodeString(cap, quote = "\"")),
                                 "knitr::kable(tab, ...)", fence), envir = child, quiet = TRUE), sep = "\n")
}
# The study root is the nearest directory above this file holding _study.yml,
# so the job renders the same from the Render button, quarto render, or
# render_job(), at any depth, with no path in this document to edit.
# To render a job you have not finished, leave a chunk out with the chunk
# option skip, giving the reason in quotes, or call hvtiRtemplates::stop_here()
# in a chunk to leave out everything below it. A draft lists each one in a
# callout; a final render refuses them, as it refuses an unresolved marker.
# ?stop_here has more.
# show_markers = FALSE: the draft banner and the warning give only the COUNT of
# open markers. A marker line could sit beside a rule naming a patient, and this
# report shows no source. The marker text goes to the console.
# box_data = FALSE: this job builds a dataset and reads none, so the box under
# the title names none; the registered "built" of an earlier build is not its data.
.job <- hvtiRtemplates:::.job_setup(SUBJECT, TYPE, envir = environment(), show_markers = FALSE, box_data = FALSE)
.root <- .job$root
.provenance_data <- list()
# The draft banners, if any, and the box under the title, after all the code above.
.job$notice
```

## Study choices

```{r}
#| label: edit-study-choices
# EDIT: the master snapshot this study is cut from: the parquet file that hvtiRdatabuild::snapshot_master() wrote.
# Its .meta.json sidecar must sit beside it. Name one dated snapshot, so a rebuild reads the same master.
MASTER <- "/path/to/snapshots/built_YYYYMMDD.parquet"

# TRUE rehashes the whole snapshot against its sidecar, which takes minutes on a
# large master. Worth it on the render that registers.
VERIFY_MASTER <- FALSE

# EDIT: a cohort list (a REDCap export or data-request CSV) kept beside the data, or NULL for a cohort the rules define.
# For example file.path(hvtiRutilities::study_dir("datasets", .root), "cohort.csv"). Only master rows the list
# names are kept. A list may carry exclude (1 to exclude) and reason columns. A list's reasons are printed in the
# report, one attrition row per distinct reason, so they must be categories (such as "Redo operation"), never free
# text, names or dates.
COHORT <- NULL

# The columns that match a cohort-list row to a master row. Dates in the list are written YYYY-MM-DD.
JOIN_BY <- c("ccfid", "dt_surg")

# EDIT: the master columns this study's dataset carries, in lower case. ID and KEY are added for you.
KEEP <- c("age", "sex", "dt_surg")

# EDIT: who is excluded, and why, in order, as condition ~ "Reason".
# A row whose condition is MISSING is NOT excluded, as SAS `if ... then delete` treats it, and the report counts
# such rows. That is the opposite of a downstream job's WHERE, which drops them, so write is.na() into a rule
# when a missing value should exclude. Rules may name patients, for example
#   ccfid %in% c("<id>", "<id>") ~ "Withdrew consent"
# and one row per patient is a rule after ordering the rows in the derive chunk's place, for example
#   duplicated(ccfid) ~ "Later operation"
# The report shows each rule's reason and counts, never its text, and the build record keeps only a hash of the
# rules, so a rule naming a patient stays in this file.
EXCLUDE <- list(is.na(dt_surg) ~ "No surgery date")

# The patient, and what makes a row unique: one row per patient unless repeated measures.
ID  <- "ccfid"
KEY <- ID

# EDIT: the name of this study's dataset, written as datasets/<DATASET_ID>.rds: lower-case letters, digits and
# underscores. A study already registered keeps the name it was registered under.
DATASET_ID <- "study_cohort"

# EDIT: pairs of columns to cross-tabulate, typically a derived column against its source, such as an event
# indicator against an indicator of its date. A missing value is a level of its own, as PROC FREQ / MISSING shows
# it. A list of character vectors, or list() for none. A cross-tab's levels are values, and a column's type or
# number of values cannot show that its labels are not identifying (a factor of dates, a patient label repeated
# in a repeated-measures dataset), so the levels and counts print in the console and never in the report. The
# report holds each pair's shape: the number of levels of each column, the cells, the cells under 5 and the
# rows with a missing value. Any column of the built dataset may be named.
CROSSTABS <- list(c("dead", "sex"))

# EDIT: the event indicator and its follow-up interval(s) in years, as the derive chunk makes them. EVENT <- NULL
# checks none.
EVENT    <- "dead"
FOLLOWUP <- "iv_dead"

# EDIT: the rows that look wrong, as condition ~ "Label", the shape of EXCLUDE. The report shows each label and
# how many rows match; the matching rows go to the console. A check may name a patient, for example
#   ccfid == "<id>" ~ "The patient queried by the surgeon"
# and a row for which a condition is missing is counted apart, never as a match. list() for none.
CHECKS <- list(
  dead == 1 & is.na(iv_dead) ~ "Event with no follow-up interval",
  iv_dead <= 0 ~ "Follow-up interval of zero or less"
)

# EDIT: the columns printed in the console for each check's matching rows. NULL prints every column.
PRINT_COLS <- c("dead", "iv_dead")

# FALSE writes the working file and registers nothing. TRUE registers it as a
# dated version of this study's "built" dataset, which every analysis job then
# reads. Render with FALSE first and read the report, which shows how this build
# differs from the version registered now, then set TRUE and render again. A draft
# prints the SHA-256 of the file it wrote in its report, and a registering render
# registers a file only if that report, beside this job, names its bytes. It stops
# when run outside a Quarto render, when no draft report is there, and when the
# report names other bytes.
REGISTER <- FALSE
```

```{r}
#| label: check-choices
# Checked before the master is read, so a bad setting fails in seconds rather
# than after a long read.
if (!is.character(DATASET_ID) || length(DATASET_ID) != 1L || !grepl("^[a-z0-9_]+$", DATASET_ID)) {
  .bd_stop("check-choices", "DATASET_ID must be lower-case letters, digits and underscores.")
}
# A dated name (_YYYYMMDD, or _YYYYMMDD_rN) belongs to a published release or a registered
# version, whose bytes must never change: the working file would be written over them.
if (grepl("_[0-9]{8}(_r[0-9]+)?$", DATASET_ID)) {
  .bd_stop("check-choices", "DATASET_ID ends in a date, as a published release or a registered version is named. ",
           "Choose a name without one.")
}
if (!is.character(KEEP) || !length(KEEP)) .bd_stop("check-choices", "KEEP is empty. Name the master columns to carry.")
if (!is.logical(REGISTER) || length(REGISTER) != 1L || is.na(REGISTER)) {
  .bd_stop("check-choices", "REGISTER must be TRUE or FALSE.")
}
if (!is.character(MASTER) || length(MASTER) != 1L) .bd_stop("check-choices", "MASTER must be one path.")
if (inherits(EXCLUDE, "formula")) EXCLUDE <- list(EXCLUDE)
if (is.character(CROSSTABS)) CROSSTABS <- list(CROSSTABS)
if (!is.list(CROSSTABS) || !all(vapply(CROSSTABS, is.character, logical(1L)))) {
  .bd_stop("check-choices", "CROSSTABS must be a list of column-name vectors, or list().")
}
if (inherits(CHECKS, "formula")) CHECKS <- list(CHECKS)
if (!is.list(CHECKS)) .bd_stop("check-choices", "CHECKS must be a list of condition ~ \"Label\", or list().")
if (!is.null(EVENT) && (!is.character(EVENT) || length(EVENT) != 1L || !is.character(FOLLOWUP) || !length(FOLLOWUP))) {
  .bd_stop("check-choices", "EVENT must be one column name and FOLLOWUP one or more, or EVENT NULL.")
}
KEEP <- tolower(KEEP)
JOIN_BY <- tolower(JOIN_BY)
ID <- tolower(ID)
KEY <- tolower(KEY)
CROSSTABS <- lapply(CROSSTABS, tolower)
```

```{r}
#| label: read-master
# The one chunk that changes when the master is read from a warehouse table
# instead of a snapshot file: everything after it sees only `d`.
.sidecar <- sub("[.]parquet$", ".meta.json", MASTER)
if (!file.exists(MASTER)) .bd_stop("read-master", "the master snapshot ", MASTER, " does not exist. Set MASTER.")
if (!file.exists(.sidecar)) {
  .bd_stop("read-master", "the master snapshot has no sidecar ", .sidecar,
           ". Snapshot the master with hvtiRdatabuild::snapshot_master(), which writes both.")
}
.meta <- jsonlite::read_json(.sidecar)
if (isTRUE(VERIFY_MASTER) && !identical(digest::digest(MASTER, algo = "sha256", file = TRUE), .meta$parquet_sha256)) {
  .bd_stop("read-master", MASTER, " does not match the SHA-256 in its sidecar. It changed after it was written; ",
           "snapshot the master again.")
}
.master <- list(file = MASTER, sha256 = .meta$parquet_sha256, rows = .meta$n_rows,
                parent_release = if (is.null(.meta$lineage$parent_release)) NA else .meta$lineage$parent_release,
                verified = isTRUE(VERIFY_MASTER))

# Read only the columns the job uses: a master can hold thousands.
.available <- names(arrow::open_dataset(MASTER))
.need <- unique(c(KEEP, ID, KEY, if (!is.null(COHORT)) JOIN_BY))
.absent <- .need[!.need %in% tolower(.available)]
if (length(.absent)) {
  .bd_stop("read-master", "column(s) ", toString(.absent), " are not in the master. Check KEEP, ID, KEY and JOIN_BY.")
}
.rule_vars <- unlist(lapply(EXCLUDE, function(rule) all.vars(rlang::f_lhs(rule))))
.cols <- .available[tolower(.available) %in% c(.need, JOIN_BY, tolower(.rule_vars))]
# !! injects the vector, which arrow selects with tidyselect; a bare external vector draws its deprecation warning.
d <- as.data.frame(arrow::read_parquet(MASTER, col_select = !!.cols))
names(d) <- tolower(names(d))
```

## Cohort

```{r}
#| label: cohort
.cut <- tryCatch(
  hvtiRtemplates::build_cohort(d, exclude = EXCLUDE, cohort = COHORT, join_by = JOIN_BY, id = ID),
  error = function(e) .bd_stop("cohort", conditionMessage(e))
)
d <- .cut$data
```

<!-- EDIT: add the study's own derived variables to the derive chunk below, the ones every analysis of this dataset needs.
     The marker sits here, not in the chunk, because a chunk holding one must be labeled edit-, and this chunk's
     label is the step name its failures report. -->

```{r}
#| label: derive
.rows_before_derive <- nrow(d)
.columns_before_derive <- names(d)

# Derived variables go here. Follow-up intervals and event indicators belong here; imputation, propensity
# scores and variables for one model belong in a vars job. For example, with
# columns your master may name differently:
#   d$iv_dead <- as.numeric(d$dt_last - d$dt_surg) / 365.25
#   d$dead    <- as.integer(!is.na(d$dt_death))

if (nrow(d) != .rows_before_derive) {
  .bd_stop("derive", "the derivations changed the number of rows from ", .rows_before_derive, " to ", nrow(d),
           ". Derive columns here and exclude rows in EXCLUDE.")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: write-built
.datasets <- hvtiRutilities::study_dir("datasets", .root)
.derived <- setdiff(names(d), .columns_before_derive)
.carry <- unique(c(ID, KEY, JOIN_BY, KEEP, .derived))
d <- d[, intersect(.carry, names(d)), drop = FALSE]
# Direct identifiers are dropped unless one is the ID or KEY, as read_job_data() drops them: ccfid, MRN,
# eMRN, Social Security numbers, patient names and contact details, by name, and a column whose
# values are shaped like SSNs whatever its name. A lookup by identifier belongs in the query above,
# never in the built a statistician reads.
.dropped <- hvtiRtemplates:::.drop_identifiers(d, ID, KEY)
d <- .dropped$data
if (length(.dropped$dropped)) message("Identifiers dropped from the built: ", toString(.dropped$dropped))
.repeats <- sum(duplicated(d[KEY]))
if (.repeats) {
  .bd_stop("write-built", .repeats, " row(s) repeat a value of KEY (", toString(KEY), "). Exclude the extra rows in ",
           "EXCLUDE, or add a column to KEY.")
}
# The working file is overwritten in place. Jobs keep reading the version registered
# last until a render with REGISTER = TRUE registers this one.
.built <- file.path(.datasets, paste0(DATASET_ID, ".rds"))
# A file a retired catalog lists is a published release, whatever its name: stop before writing over it.
.catalog <- file.path(.datasets, "dataset-catalog.yml")
.released <- if (file.exists(.catalog)) {
  unlist(lapply(yaml::read_yaml(.catalog)$datasets, function(ds) lapply(ds$releases, function(r) r$file)))
}
if (basename(.built) %in% .released) {
  .bd_stop("write-built", basename(.built), " is a published release in dataset-catalog.yml, and is never written over. ",
           "Choose another DATASET_ID.")
}
saveRDS(d, .built)

# The build record sits beside the working file, as <stem>.build.yml. Registering
# the file claims it only if built_sha256 is the hash of these bytes, and moves it
# beside the dated version. It is never rendered and never committed, and it holds
# no key and no data value: the rules are recorded as their hash, and the rules
# themselves stay in this job, which is how the cut can be made again.
.sha256_text <- function(x) digest::digest(x, algo = "sha256", serialize = FALSE)
.cohort_rules <- list(
  cohort_sha256 = if (is.null(COHORT)) NULL else digest::digest(COHORT, algo = "sha256", file = TRUE),
  join_by = JOIN_BY, keep = KEEP, id = ID, key = KEY,
  exclude = vapply(EXCLUDE, function(rule) paste(deparse(rule), collapse = " "), "")
)
# The job's path within the study. A purled script run with source() has no file to name.
.job_path <- if (is.null(.in)) {
  "(not rendered: run as a script)"
} else {
  .job_dir <- normalizePath(dirname(.in), winslash = "/")
  .root_dir <- normalizePath(.root, winslash = "/")
  .job_rel <- substring(.job_dir, nchar(.root_dir) + 2L)
  if (nzchar(.job_rel)) file.path(.job_rel, .job_file) else .job_file
}
.record <- list(
  schema = 1L,
  built_sha256 = digest::digest(.built, algo = "sha256", file = TRUE),
  job = .job_path,
  view = basename(.master$file),
  # A snapshot is pinned by its bytes; its modification time is when it was taken.
  as_of = format(file.mtime(.master$file), "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", tz = "UTC"),
  cohort_sha256 = .sha256_text(yaml::as.yaml(.cohort_rules)),
  # This job applies no study corrections overlay yet, so its derivations always follow the (absent) overlay.
  overlay_sha256 = NULL,
  derived_after_overlay = TRUE,
  master = .master,
  settings = list(cohort = COHORT, join_by = JOIN_BY, keep = KEEP, id = ID, key = KEY, dataset_id = DATASET_ID),
  attrition = .cut$attrition,
  hvtiRtemplates = as.character(utils::packageVersion("hvtiRtemplates"))
)
.record_file <- file.path(.datasets, paste0(DATASET_ID, ".build.yml"))
yaml::write_yaml(.record, .record_file)
```

## Checks

These checks read the dataset this render has just written. They report counts only: the rows behind a count,
the patients on one side of the rebuild only and the levels of each cross-tab are printed in the console, so
run the chunks in an interactive session to read them. A finding changes nothing and blocks nothing. A check that cannot run,
because a column it names is missing or a condition does not evaluate, stops the render, as a bad `EXCLUDE` rule
does: a build whose checks did not run is never registered. A finding becomes a correction to the master, a rule
in `EXCLUDE`, or a fix to the derive chunk; then render again, and register once the checks
read right. A draft's report prints the SHA-256 of the file it wrote, and a registering render registers only a
file whose bytes that report names, so register from a render, never from chunks run by hand.

### What this rebuild changed

```{r}
#| label: rebuild
#| results: asis
# unnumbered: its two tables are child chunks with their own labels and captions
# The baseline is the version registered now for the study's declared dataset, read
# with read_built(working = FALSE) and bound to this build here, never looked up by a
# helper on its own. review_built() resolves its file from _study.yml and not from
# DATASET_ID, so in a comparison build it would review the declared file while every
# check below reads this one. working = FALSE is explicit: with nothing registered,
# or with HVTI_DATA = "working", read_built() serves the working file, and the
# comparison would be this file against itself.
.cfg <- hvtiRutilities::study_config(.root, require_data = FALSE)
.declared <- .cfg$built
.found <- if (!is.null(.declared)) hvtiRtemplates:::.manifest_find(.root, source = .declared)
.comparison <- NULL
if (is.null(.found)) {
  .rebuild_state <- "Nothing is registered for this study yet, so there is no version to compare this build against."
} else {
  # .provenance_read() stops if the registered version changes while it is read. Its record is not shown: it
  # follows HVTI_DATA, and would name the working file under a working read where this read the registered one.
  .baseline_read <- tryCatch(
    hvtiRtemplates:::.provenance_read("study", .cfg, function() hvtiRutilities::read_built(.cfg, working = FALSE),
                                      role = "baseline"),
    error = function(e) .bd_stop("rebuild", conditionMessage(e))
  )
  .baseline <- .baseline_read$value
  # A SAS-built version may name its columns in upper case; this build's names are lower case.
  names(.baseline) <- tolower(names(.baseline))
  .rebuild_state <- if (identical(.declared, basename(.built))) {
    paste0("A rebuild of the study dataset: ", basename(.built), " against its registered version ",
           .found$version_file, ".")
  } else {
    paste0("A comparison build: ", basename(.built), " is not the study dataset. It is compared against the study ",
           "dataset ", .declared, ", registered as ", .found$version_file, ", which this build leaves unchanged.")
  }
  # compare_built() joins on one column. A KEY of several columns is joined on all of them.
  .join <- function(x) {
    if (length(KEY) == 1L) return(x)
    x$.bd_key <- do.call(paste, c(unname(as.list(x[KEY])), sep = "\r"))
    # A missing part leaves the key missing, which compare_built() refuses, rather than the text "NA".
    x$.bd_key[!stats::complete.cases(x[KEY])] <- NA
    x
  }
  .id <- if (length(KEY) == 1L) KEY else ".bd_key"
  # read_built() reads a logical column as integer and drops a labeled column's value labels, so this
  # build is read the same way: otherwise every logical derivation reads "type changed" and its values,
  # the thing a rebuild check is for, are never compared. The checks below read the data as written.
  .as_read <- d
  .as_read[] <- lapply(.as_read, function(x) {
    if (is.logical(x)) return(as.integer(x))
    if (!inherits(x, "haven_labelled")) return(x)
    out <- as.vector(x)
    attr(out, "label") <- attr(x, "label")
    out
  })
  # A KEY the registered version lacks cannot be joined on: report it and compare nothing, as a first build does.
  # Registering still proceeds, since that is how a changed key reaches the study. Any other failure stops.
  .key_gone <- setdiff(KEY, names(.baseline))
  if (length(.key_gone)) {
    .rebuild_state <- paste0(.rebuild_state, " The KEY (", toString(KEY), ") has changed since the registered version, ",
                             "which lacks ", toString(.key_gone), ", so nothing is compared.")
  } else {
    .comparison <- tryCatch(hvtiRdatabuild::compare_built(.join(.baseline), .join(.as_read), id = .id),
                            error = function(e) .bd_stop("rebuild", conditionMessage(e)))
    .rows <- attr(.comparison, "rows")
    # The patients on one side only are identifiers: the console has them, the report their count.
    for (.side in c("only_oracle", "only_r")) {
      .ids <- .rows[[.side]]
      cat("\n", if (.side == "only_oracle") "In the registered version only" else "In this build only", ": ",
          length(.ids), " row(s)\n", sep = "", file = stderr())
      if (length(.ids)) cat(utils::head(.ids, 100L), sep = "\n", file = stderr())
      if (length(.ids) > 100L) cat("... ", length(.ids) - 100L, " more not shown\n", sep = "", file = stderr())
    }
  }
}
cat(.rebuild_state, "\n")
# Per column: identical, within tolerance or differs, with how many rows differ and by
# how much. It is never collapsed into a pass or a fail: a difference is read, not counted.
# The tables are shown only when there is a comparison, so a study with nothing registered shows no empty caption.
if (!is.null(.comparison)) {
  .rows_tab <- data.frame(
    Item = c("Rows in the registered version", "Rows in this build", "Rows in both",
             "In the registered version only", "In this build only"),
    Value = c(.rows$n_oracle, .rows$n_r, .rows$n_common, length(.rows$only_oracle), length(.rows$only_r))
  )
  .verdicts <- c(absent_in_r = "in the registered version only", absent_in_sas = "in this build only",
                 type_mismatch = "type changed")
  .columns_tab <- data.frame(
    Column = .comparison$variable,
    Verdict = ifelse(.comparison$verdict %in% names(.verdicts), .verdicts[.comparison$verdict], .comparison$verdict),
    `Rows differing` = .comparison$n_differ,
    `Largest difference` = signif(.comparison$max_abs_diff, 4),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
  .bd_table(.rows_tab, "tbl-rebuild-rows", "Rows in the registered version and in this build, joined on the dataset's key")
  .bd_table(.columns_tab, "tbl-rebuild-columns", "Each column of the rows in both, compared by value")
}
```

### Cross-tabs

```{r}
#| label: crosstabs
#| results: asis
# unnumbered: its table is a child chunk with its own label and caption
# The levels of a cross-tab are values, so the full table of each pair, levels and counts, goes to the
# console on stderr(), which knitr does not collect, as the rows behind a named check do. The report holds
# each pair's shape and no label. A small cell is flagged in the console, never suppressed.
.small <- 5L
if (!length(CROSSTABS)) cat("No cross-tabs are named in CROSSTABS.\n")
.shapes <- vector("list", length(CROSSTABS))
for (.i in seq_along(CROSSTABS)) {
  .pair <- CROSSTABS[[.i]]
  for (.col in .pair) {
    if (!.col %in% names(d)) .bd_stop("crosstabs", "CROSSTABS names ", .col, ", which the built dataset does not have.")
  }
  .tab <- tryCatch(hvtiRutilities::proc_freq(d, .pair, missing = TRUE),
                   error = function(e) .bd_stop("crosstabs", conditionMessage(e)))
  .tab <- .tab[, intersect(c(.pair, "Frequency", "Percent"), names(.tab)), drop = FALSE]
  .tab$Small <- ifelse(.tab$Frequency > 0 & .tab$Frequency < .small, paste("under", .small), "")
  .tab[.pair] <- lapply(.tab[.pair], function(x) ifelse(is.na(x), "(missing)", as.character(x)))
  .by <- paste(.pair, collapse = " by ")
  cat("\n", .by, "\n", sep = "", file = stderr())
  cat(utils::capture.output(print(.tab, row.names = FALSE)), sep = "\n", file = stderr())
  # A missing value counts as a level, as it does in the table.
  .nlevels <- vapply(.pair, function(col) length(unique(d[[col]])), 0L)
  .shapes[[.i]] <- data.frame(
    Pair = .by, Levels = paste(.nlevels, collapse = " x "), Cells = prod(.nlevels),
    `Cells under 5` = sum(.tab$Frequency > 0 & .tab$Frequency < .small),
    Missing = sum(!stats::complete.cases(d[.pair])), check.names = FALSE
  )
}
if (length(.shapes)) {
  .bd_table(do.call(rbind, .shapes), "tbl-crosstabs",
            "Each cross-tab's shape, with a missing value as a level of its own; the levels and counts are in the console",
            row.names = FALSE)
}
```

### Follow-up

```{r}
#| label: followup
#| results: asis
# unnumbered: its two tables are child chunks with their own labels and captions
# identifier = NULL: the report holds aggregates only. The suspicious rows the check
# finds go to the console, without an identifier, for the author to look at.
if (is.null(EVENT)) {
  cat("No follow-up pair is named in EVENT.\n")
} else {
  .fc <- tryCatch(hvtiRutilities::followup_check(d, event = EVENT, followup = FOLLOWUP, identifier = NULL),
                  error = function(e) .bd_stop("followup", conditionMessage(e)))
  .bd_table(.fc$cohort, "tbl-followup-cohort", "Patients by event status")
  .bd_table(.fc$intervals, "tbl-followup-intervals", "Each follow-up interval", digits = 3)
  # review lists at most 25 rows; n_suspicious counts them all.
  .n_suspicious <- attr(.fc, "n_suspicious")
  cat("\n", .n_suspicious, " row(s) look suspicious, listed in the console.\n", sep = "")
  if (nrow(.fc$review)) cat(utils::capture.output(print(.fc$review, row.names = FALSE)), sep = "\n", file = stderr())
  if (.n_suspicious > nrow(.fc$review)) {
    cat("... ", .n_suspicious - nrow(.fc$review), " more not shown\n", sep = "", file = stderr())
  }
}
```

### Named checks

```{r}
#| label: tbl-checks
#| tbl-cap: "Rows matching each named check; the rows themselves are in the console"
# proc_print() writes the matching rows to stderr(), which a render does not knit, and
# returns one count per check, which is all this report shows.
if (length(CHECKS)) {
  .checked <- tryCatch(hvtiRutilities::proc_print(d, where = CHECKS, var = PRINT_COLS),
                       error = function(e) .bd_stop("tbl-checks", conditionMessage(e)))
  knitr::kable(.checked, col.names = c("Check", "Rows matching", "Undecided (missing)"))
} else {
  knitr::kable(data.frame(Check = "No checks are named in CHECKS."))
}
```

## Register

```{r}
#| label: register
# The dated version registered from `built` now, from the study's manifest: NULL when none is.
.current_version <- function(built) {
  if (is.null(built)) NULL else hvtiRtemplates:::.manifest_find(.root, source = built)$version_file
}
# require_data = FALSE: a study that has registered no dataset yet is the normal first build.
.registered <- hvtiRutilities::study_config(.root, require_data = FALSE)
.version_before <- .current_version(.registered$built)
.register_step <- "Working file only: nothing registered"
# A new study's first build is named in _study.yml with no version registered, so a draft job can
# read it before it is registered (design 2026-10-23, section 7.1). Registering stays a separate
# step: REGISTER = TRUE, or hvtiRutilities::update_manifest().
.other_file <- !is.null(.registered$built) && !identical(.registered$built, basename(.built))
# A render with a skipped chunk or a stop_here() did not run every check, so it declares nothing, prints no
# review hash and registers nothing. Outside a render there is no file to be partial.
.partial <- !is.null(.in) && length(hvtiRtemplates:::.partial_state$points) > 0L
if (!REGISTER && .partial) {
  .register_step <- "Partial render: nothing declared, reviewed or registered"
} else if (!REGISTER && is.null(.registered$built)) {
  hvtiRutilities::declare_data(.root, built = basename(.built), key = KEY)
  .register_step <- "Declared as the study dataset: nothing registered"
} else if (!REGISTER && .other_file) {
  # A comparison build, such as an R rebuild beside a SAS-built dataset, is allowed to write its working
  # file: it declares nothing and registers nothing, and the report says the study's dataset is unchanged.
  .register_step <- paste0("Working file only: the study's dataset is still ", .registered$built,
                           ", so this build was not declared or registered")
}
if (REGISTER) {
  # Running chunks by hand can leave any check out, and no report would show it.
  if (is.null(.in)) {
    .bd_stop("register", "this is not a Quarto render, and running chunks by hand can leave a check out. ",
             "Render the job instead: with REGISTER <- FALSE first, then with REGISTER <- TRUE.")
  }
  if (.partial) {
    .bd_stop("register", "this render is partial (a chunk is skipped or stop_here() is set), so its checks did not all run ",
             "and it was not registered. Remove each skip and stop_here(), draft again, then register.")
  }
  # A study registered under another file cannot take this one as its dataset.
  if (.other_file) {
    # Name a DATASET_ID only for a file this job could have written: a dated name is a retired
    # catalog release, whose bytes must never be overwritten.
    .own <- grepl("^[a-z0-9_]+[.]rds$", .registered$built) && !grepl("_[0-9]{8}(_r[0-9]+)?[.]rds$", .registered$built)
    .bd_stop("register", "this study's dataset is registered as ", .registered$built, ", and this job writes ",
             basename(.built), ". ",
             if (.own) {
               paste0("Set DATASET_ID to \"", sub("[.]rds$", "", .registered$built), "\" if that file is this job's, or ")
             } else {
               ""
             },
             "move the study to this job's file deliberately.")
  }
  # The draft's report is the record of the review: the draft prints the SHA-256 of the bytes it wrote, and only
  # a draft that rendered to the end leaves its HTML beside this job. The report is the job's own output file.
  .draft_html <- file.path(dirname(.in), sub("[.]qmd$", ".html", .job_file))
  .draft_report <- if (file.exists(.draft_html)) readLines(.draft_html, warn = FALSE)
  if (is.null(.draft_report)) {
    .bd_stop("register", "no draft report was found beside this job (", sub("[.]qmd$", ".html", .job_file), "), so the ",
             "build was not registered. Render with REGISTER <- FALSE, read the report, then render again with ",
             "REGISTER <- TRUE.")
  }
  # The working file is hashed again here, not trusted from the build record: the file registered is the file
  # read now. Nothing runs between this and the registration but choosing the call.
  .built_now <- digest::digest(.built, algo = "sha256", file = TRUE)
  if (!identical(.built_now, .record$built_sha256)) {
    .bd_stop("register", "the working file changed after this render wrote it (another job or render wrote ",
             basename(.built), "), so it was not registered. Render a draft again, read it, then register.")
  }
  if (!any(grepl(.built_now, .draft_report, fixed = TRUE))) {
    .bd_stop("register", "the draft report names other bytes than this build (a draft and a registering render under ",
             "different R versions always differ, since saveRDS records the version; a registering render's own report ",
             "names none), so it was not registered. Render with REGISTER <- FALSE, read the report, then render again ",
             "with REGISTER <- TRUE.")
  }
  .register_step <- tryCatch({
    if (is.null(.registered$built)) {
      hvtiRutilities::register_data(.root, built = basename(.built))
      "Registered as the study dataset"
    } else {
      # update_manifest() finds the study from the working directory.
      .owd <- setwd(.root)
      .update <- tryCatch(hvtiRutilities::update_manifest(dataset = "study"), finally = setwd(.owd))
      switch(.update$action[[1L]],
        registered = ,
        migrated = "Registered as a new version of the study dataset",
        unchanged = "Unchanged since the version registered: nothing to do",
        # skipped or missing: nothing was registered, and the render must not read as if it had been.
        .bd_stop("register", "update_manifest() registered nothing (", .update$action[[1L]], "): ", .update$detail[[1L]])
      )
    }
  }, error = function(e) {
    if (startsWith(conditionMessage(e), "bd: ")) stop(e)
    .bd_stop("register", "registering the dataset stopped: ", conditionMessage(e))
  })
}
.version_after <- .current_version(hvtiRutilities::study_config(.root, require_data = FALSE)$built)
```

## Report

```{r}
#| label: tbl-report-source
#| tbl-cap: "Run mode, master snapshot, row counts and dataset registration for this render"
# A draft that ran to the end prints the SHA-256 of the file it wrote: this report is the record of the review, and
# a registering render registers only a file whose bytes it names. A partial draft and a registering render print none.
.review_row <- !REGISTER && !.partial
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Item = c("Mode", "Master snapshot", "Master SHA-256", "Rehashed this render", "Master parent release",
           "Rows in the dataset", "Patients", "Columns", "Study dataset before", "Study dataset after", "Registration",
           if (.review_row) "Build reviewed (sha256)"),
  Value = c(if (REGISTER) "Register" else "Working file only", basename(.master$file), .master$sha256,
            if (.master$verified) "yes" else "no", as.character(.master$parent_release), nrow(d),
            length(unique(d[[ID]])), ncol(d),
            if (is.null(.version_before)) "none" else .version_before,
            if (is.null(.version_after)) "none" else .version_after, .register_step,
            if (.review_row) .record$built_sha256)
))
```

### Columns

```{r}
#| label: tbl-report-columns
#| tbl-cap: "Type, missing count and range of each column"
# Aggregates only: the type, missing count and range of each column. The ID, KEY
# and JOIN_BY columns get no range: a range of identifiers is two identifiers,
# and a JOIN_BY date range is two patients' dates.
.no_range <- c(ID, KEY, JOIN_BY)
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Column = names(d),
  Type = vapply(d, function(x) class(x)[[1L]], ""),
  Missing = vapply(d, function(x) sum(is.na(x)), 0L),
  Range = vapply(names(d), function(col) {
    x <- d[[col]]
    if (col %in% .no_range || !is.numeric(x) || all(is.na(x))) {
      ""
    } else {
      paste(format(range(x, na.rm = TRUE), digits = 4), collapse = " to ")
    }
  }, ""),
  row.names = NULL
))
```

```{r}
#| label: about-run
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
# unnumbered: the section is a table the package draws, headed "About this run"
# require_data = FALSE: a first draft that is partial declares no dataset, and still reports its run.
.about_cfg <- hvtiRutilities::study_config(start = .root, require_data = FALSE)
cat(hvtiRtemplates:::.about_run(.job$run, cfg = .about_cfg, envir = environment()))
```
